name: Acquired Factor XI Deficiency

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Acquired Factor XI Deficiency Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) not corrected by mixing studies
Reduced Factor XI activity levels in plasma
Detection of acquired Factor XI inhibitors (autoantibodies) by Bethesda assay or similar
Exclusion of congenital Factor XI deficiency by patient history and family studies
Clinical evidence of bleeding disproportionate to trauma or surgery

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of prolonged aPTT not corrected by mixing studies, reduced Factor XI activity, and detection of acquired Factor XI inhibitors
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of congenital Factor XI deficiency and other coagulopathies.

searchTerms: bleeding from mucous membranes without injury
spontaneous bleeding in mouth or nose

pathognomonic.symptomName: Postoperative hemorrhage disproportionate to surgical trauma
searchTerms: bleeding after surgery more than expected
minor cuts bleed for a long time
prolonged bleeding from minor skin injuries

laboratory: Prolonged activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) not corrected by mixing studies
Presence of Factor XI inhibitors detected by Bethesda assay
imaging: Imaging to identify bleeding sites such as CT or MRI for intracranial or retroperitoneal hemorrhage
genetic: No known genetic mutations associated with acquired form; distinguishes from congenital Factor XI deficiency
other: Clinical history of bleeding without prior personal or family history of bleeding disorders

distinguishingFeatures: Normal mixing study correction of aPTT
Prolonged aPTT with Factor VIII inhibitor presence

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe bleeding without prior history
Prolonged aPTT uncorrected by mixing studies
Failure to respond to standard hemostatic treatments
references: Franchini M, Lippi G. Acquired factor XI inhibitors: a systematic review. Semin Thromb Hemost. 2011;37(7):767-773.
Orphanet: Acquired factor XI deficiency - ORPHA599507
Katz U, et al. Acquired factor XI inhibitors: clinical and laboratory features. Haemophilia. 2006;12(6):637-641.
